The Restoration of the World

The Collapse shattered the structure of reality.

The vessels that once focused the light of creation burst apart.
The systems that held the world together fractured.
Fragments of existence drifted away from one another.

Yet the ancient traditions of the world hold that the breaking of the vessels was not the end of the story.

It was the beginning of something else.

That something is known as Tikkun.

The Meaning of Tikkun

In the oldest surviving traditions, Tikkun means repair, restoration, or mending.

It is the belief that even after the structure of the world breaks, the fragments still contain the possibility of being made whole again.

The light that once filled the shattered vessels did not vanish.

It scattered.

Small sparks of that original harmony now exist throughout the fragments of reality.

Wherever those sparks are gathered, protected, and strengthened, the world moves one step closer to restoration.

Sparks in the Fragments

According to ancient teachings, every broken fragment of reality contains pieces of the original light.

These sparks appear in many forms:

• communities struggling to rebuild
• knowledge preserved from the age before the Collapse
• places where the forces of the world remain in balance
• individuals who refuse to surrender to despair

Each of these represents a small piece of the harmony that once existed.

When people nurture these sparks, they participate in the work of restoration.

Tikkun in the Age of Fragments

In the modern age, the idea of Tikkun has taken on a practical meaning.

Across the world, individuals and factions attempt to repair the damage left by the Collapse.

They stabilize dangerous regions.
They rebuild shattered infrastructure.
They protect communities.
They rediscover lost knowledge.

Each of these actions contributes to the gradual restoration of the world.

Though the task is enormous, every repaired fragment strengthens the possibility that the world can heal.

The Work of Many Hands

Tikkun is not something that can be accomplished through a single act.

It is the result of countless decisions made across generations.

Every explorer who maps a dangerous region…
Every community that rebuilds after disaster…
Every faction that chooses restoration over exploitation…

All of them participate in the same long effort.

The restoration of the world is not the responsibility of heroes alone.

It belongs to everyone who believes the fragments can still become something greater.

The Opposition to Tikkun

Not all forces in the world support restoration.

Darkness spreads through instability and suffering.

Some factions exploit chaos for their own gain.

Others believe the world cannot be repaired and see no reason to try.

These forces make the path toward restoration difficult.

Yet every act of Tikkun pushes back against the spread of corruption.

The Hope of the World

Despite the damage left by the Collapse, many believe that the fragments of reality still contain the pattern needed to rebuild what was lost.

If the broken lenses of creation can be brought back into balance…

If the leylines can be restored…

If enough fragments of the world can be stabilized…

Then the deeper systems of reality may begin functioning again.

No one knows whether the world will ever fully return to what it once was.

But many believe it can become something whole again.

Your Role in Tikkun

In Bad Eden, your characters and faction are part of this ancient effort.

Every hex you stabilize…
Every community you help rebuild…
Every threat you confront…

…becomes part of the work of restoration.

The campaign is not only a story about survival in a broken world.

It is a story about whether that world can be repaired.

In Simple Terms

Tikkun is the belief that the shattered world can be restored.

By gathering the scattered sparks of harmony and repairing the fragments of reality, people slowly rebuild what was lost.

Every action taken by the players becomes part of that restoration.
